messages.subject: Sumstats Flags
parts:
To all, 

I was working through a GWAS by subtraction and I am not sure what flags to use.  

I was using Howard et al.'s 2019 depression GWAS excluding 23andMe - a meta analysis of UKB broad depression (analyzed de novo I think using BGENIE) and Wray et al's 2017 PGC depression GWAS (minus the UKB cohort to avoid duplication).  I cannot determine Wray's method of analysis from the published paper or supplement but her meta-analysis may have included Ripke et al's earlier PGC GWAS which used logistic regression.   

Would Howard's meta-analysis GWAS then come under the category in the flow-chart of Meta-analysis of binary and continuous (as meta-analysis of GWASs using both logistics and linear regression) or some other category, for Sumstats flag? 

Thanks for any help you can give me in this!

Dan

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Sumstats Flags
parts:
Hi Dan, 

My understanding is that the broad depression phenotype still reflects a case/control trait just broadly defined (though i could see how the naming of the variable would lead someone to think that it reflects a continuous measure like from the PHQ-9 in UKB for example). In this case then, this reflects a meta-analysis of two case/control traits (UKB and PGC), and since the column headers for the Howard et al. summary stats from the PGC website including 23andMe reads LogOR and StdErrLogOR you would set se.logit = T for sumstats. 

Best, 
  Andrew
